topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing introduces grating lobes, affecting coverage patterns and capacity. Adaptive beamforming mitigates this by optimizing beam steering and shaping, minimizing interference and maximizing signal-to-noise ratio. Optimal spacing balances beamforming gain and grating lobe suppression.
reference_context: Ka-band satellites use spot beam coverage, allowing frequency reuse operation, and high throughput satellites enable broadband services.
